# The statmodels7 package {#sec-statmodels7}

The chapters so far built the parts a regression model is made of: the links
of @sec-links, the distributions of @sec-distributions7, the optimizers of
@sec-optimizers7, the constrained parameters of @sec-parameters7, the bases
of @sec-basis7, the penalties of @sec-penalties7 and the model terms of
@sec-modelterms7. `statmodels7` is the layer that fits a model out of them.

What it fits is a distributional regression. An ordinary regression writes a
linear predictor for the mean and holds the rest of the distribution
constant across observations; here every parameter of the response
distribution carries an equation of its own, so a scale, a shape or a
zero-inflation probability is modeled by the same machinery and with the same
terms as a mean. One formula carries all of those equations, the terms they
name are assembled into a penalized likelihood, and the smoothing parameters
and prior scales the terms leave free are estimated from the data.

@sec-statmod-model presents the model: the formula with its equations
separated by bars, the scale each equation is written on, the specification
built from it, and what a fit keeps. @sec-statmod-inner presents the
penalized fit: the objective, the scoring step and the augmented
decomposition it is solved through, the blocks that move with their own
coefficients, the blocks whose penalty has a kink and are fitted apart, and
the rule that ends the loop. @sec-statmod-outer presents the second
estimation problem sitting outside the first, the hyperparameters the terms
leave free: the marginal criteria and their exact derivatives, the
prediction-error criteria, the path a penalty with a kink is swept along, and
the effective degrees of freedom a criterion is charged against.
@sec-statmod-structural presents the terms that rewrite the likelihood
rather than adding to it, and what a fit has to compute for them.
@sec-statmod-verdict presents the two questions that bracket a fit, where it
begins and whether the point it reports is the one the model asks for.
@sec-statmod-reading presents what a fit answers when it is read: the two
variances and the intervals built on them, which likelihood is reported,
prediction at new data, and simulation from the model.
@sec-statmod-practice closes the chapter with two models fitted and read from
end to end.
